This is the third version of this circuit for CroyTone Audio and each time it has been refined and perfected to sound better and better! From edgy 60s style fuzz to thicker more aggressive 70s style fuzz, The Camper Fuzz utilizes flexible tone controls and carefully designed gain staging to allow for a large amount of flexibility. If you love the sounds of classic fuzzes from the 60s and 70s, this is the perfect fuzz for your rig! Available for free worldwide shipping. Full demo videos available on the website!".

sources.description: 136 likes, 15 comments - croytone_audio on October 16, 2024: "After more than a year of preparation, opening a shop in a new country and navigating the challenges of doing all of this in a language I am not very good at, I am extremely excited to announce the release of the first three effects pedals from the new CroyTone Audio Technologies Japan!!!! A ton of work went into these three fuzz pedals and I am extremely proud of the result! The Camper Fuzz, Hae Fuzz and Suzumebachi Fuzz are three distinct flavors of everything I love about fuzz pedals. The Camper Fuzz is the third iteration of my very first circuit I designed back in 2016. Everything I love about vintage style fuzzes in a more consistent and versatile package. From buzzy 60s fuzz tones to loud and heavy 70s sounds, the Camper Fuzz can do it all and more! The Hae is a continuation of an octave fuzz circuit I have been working on for years. Loud, brash and cutting, this fuzz can do all the screaming tones I love about 80s and 90s alternative and shoegaze fuzz. Strong octave and ring mod type tones are available with lots of tonal flexibility and PLENTY of volume. The Suzumebachi Fuzz is a newer design that comes from my love of stacking fuzzes to get a HUGE and thick fuzz tone. Massive doomy wall of sound fuzz tones are available as well as spitting, percussive gated tones. I’m so happy to finally get these out into the world and will begin shipping them out next week. Free shipping on all three pedals in Japan and the US! Available for purchase on my website! And thank you to the amazing @ryejol for designing the artwork on these pedals!".

sources.description: The Cunningham Amps MK 1.6 Fuzz is a high-quality, vintage-voiced fuzz made by hand in New Zealand that blends the line between a MK 1.5' Tone Bender and Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face.
sources.snippet: Cunningham Amps MK 1.6 Fuzz (Ge) - Delicious Audio
sources.bodyExcerpt: Cunningham Amps MK 1.6 Fuzz (Ge) | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Cunningham Amps MK 1.6 Fuzz (Ge) Updated Jun. 9, 2025 | by Paolo De Gregorio The Cunningham Amps MK 1.6 Fuzz is a high-quality, vintage-voiced fuzz made by hand in New Zealand that blends the line between a MK 1.5′ Tone Bender and Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face. The Attack knob sets the amount of fuzz and Level controls the overall output, which ranges from soft to way more than you need, allowing you to hit hard your amp’s input stage, for extra saturation. A Gain Mode switch provides three gain settings: Low is a slightly brighter boost setting, while Med and High progressively add more gain and fuzz, with the latter sounding fuller and juicier. Cunningham Amps MK 1.6, Builder’s Notes The MK 1.6 Silicon Fuzz is hand crafted effect pedal based on classic fuzz circuits of the mid-60s. The closest ancestors are the fabled ‘MK 1.5’ Tone Bender and Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face. This model includes a few added touches to enhance playability in the modern world. The circuit is built upon a hand etched board with the highest quality components and an obsessive attention to detail. The MK 1.6 Silicon Fuzz is both battery powered and includes a DC in power socket (standard centre negative, 2.1mm plug). The battery is disconnected from the circuit when DC plug inserted so you can leave hooked up on your board. Each Pedal is built by hand, one at a time, and individually voiced to optimize its specially selected pair of transistors. This means no two pedals are exactly the same – they all have unique attributes and components are chosen to enhance the sonic qualities of each circuit. The controls are simple but highly effective – ‘Attack’ dials up the fuzz and ‘Level’ sets the overall output of the effect, which ranges from soft to sonic destruction. The MK 1.6 is designed to provide a high level of output when desired and is capable of a significant volume boost – this fuzz will not disappear in the mix when engaged. Raising the level also hits the input of your amp harder and interacts with tube preamp stages to produce beautiful overtones and a wide range of overdrive and distortion tones through to raging fuzz. The pedal provides a vast tonal palette to play with and subtle changes in pick attack and tweaks to your guitar’s volume and tone controls offer up unlimited avenues for expression. The Gain Mode switch provides three separate gain settings for the pedal. Low is a boost setting with Med and High progressively adding more gain and fuzz. Lower gain is also a tad brighter, high is fat and juicy. Each setting imparts its own special character and greatly adds to the versatility of the pedal in response to different musical situations, guitars, amps etc. Wherever you set it, be prepared for scintillating boosted fuzz tones! All pedals come complete with a handmade padded carry case, signed and numbered certificate of authenticity and instruction card. sources.bodyExcerpt: Cunningham Amps Supa Fuzz | Guitar Pedal Demo — Edge of Breakup 0 Skip to Content LATEST VIDEOS ABOUT Join the Email List Open Menu Close Menu Open Menu Close Menu LATEST VIDEOS ABOUT Join the Email List LATEST VIDEOS ABOUT Join the Email List Cunningham Amps Supa Fuzz | Guitar Pedal Demo Guitar Pedals Jul 26 Written By Edge of Breakup . Cunningham Amps Supa Fuzz: Handmade New Zealand fuzz. A shell-pink relic Kauer. Lollar Sixty-Four single coils. A 5-watt tweed Princeton pushing a re-coned vintage Jensen into the room. And a photocell Uni-Vibe swirling through all of it. Welcome back to Edge of Breakup. The Cunningham Amps Supa Fuzz runs into the Kauer Guitars Electroliner — Lollar Sixty-Four Stratocaster pickups — feeding a vintage 1957 Fender Tweed Princeton 5F2-A with a re-coned vintage Jensen P12Q, with the JAM Pedals RetroVibe MK.4 along for the ride. The Cunningham Supa Fuzz is Auckland builder Tim Cunningham's faithful interpretation of the legendary Sola Sound Supa Fuzz — the circuit that sits between a Tone Bender and a Fuzz Face in character, used to define British rock tone in the mid-to-late 1960s. Tim builds each Supa Fuzz by hand, one at a time, in a heavy-duty sand-cast Olivetti-style enclosure that nods directly to the original hardware. Each pedal is individually voiced to its specific trio of NOS germanium transistors — no two are the same. Explored from cranked Attack with Volume at amp unity (00:17), boosting fuzz volume to slam the amp into compression from 01:11, and Attack and Volume both maxed at 03:03, with guitar volume lowered for clarity at 03:37. The 1957 Fender Princeton 5F2-A is about as stripped-down and honest an amp platform as exists — single 6V6 power tube, 12AX7 preamp, 5Y3 rectifier, 5-watt Class A circuit with a smooth negative feedback loop keeping the breakup warm and musical. This unit has been fitted with a re-coned vintage Jensen P12Q in place of the original 8" speaker — an alnico-magnet, mid-focused 12" that was found in some of the most revered tweed-era American amps, giving a bigger, fuller low end and warm upper-mid bite. The Lollar Sixty-Four Stratocaster set brings pre-CBS 1964 character — scatter-wound, wax-potted, Alnico 5 magnets degaussed to vintage spec. Prominent mids, clear treble, full piano-like attack — everything the classic Fuzz Face circuit was designed to work with. The JAM Pedals RetroVibe MK.4 joins from 04:08 — the latest generation of JAM's celebrated all-analog Uni-Vibe, staying true to the photocell-and-bulb topology of the original 1960s units while adding tap tempo, a ramping function, and expression pedal control. Built in Athens, Greece. This is a rig built for feel, not features. Every element in the chain earns its place. 🎛️ Cunningham Amps: https://www.cunninghamamps.co.nz 🎸 Kauer Guitars: https://www.kauerguitars.com 🎛️ JAM Pedals: https://www.jampedals.com Subscribe for more boutique tone explorations. 🎸 Kauer Guitars Electroliner | Lollar Sixty-Four Stratocaster Set 🎛️ Cunningham Amps Supa Fuzz | JAM Pedals RetroVibe MK.4 🔊 Vintage 1957 Fender Tweed Princeton 5F2-A | Re-coned Vintage Jensen P12Q Edge of Breakup . sources.bodyExcerpt: Danelectro Daddy O DO-1 Overdrive - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Danelectro Daddy O DO-1 Overdrive Posted By Pedal of the Day on Thursday, May 1, 2025 in Danelectro, Overdrive / Distortion | 3 comments --> --> The Danelectro Cool Cat Stereo Chorus and Dan-Echo Delay Echo are two of the coolest pedals that have ever existed, right? That said, today’s pedal is often in any conversation involving those two as well, as they all come from the same classic lineup. The Daddy O DO-1 Overdrive doesn’t just have a rad-sounding name – it has a ton of rad-sounding sounds inside, as well… The Danelectro Daddy-O is an overdrive pedal that emulates classic tube-amp distortion. You get the standard Volume and O Drive controls, along with individual attenuation of the Bass, Middle and Treble frequencies. This creates an unusually high degree of tone shaping, letting you conjure up a variety of vintage overdrives , including British Stacks, Texas Blues and even some higher gain tones with ease. The wide range on these controls really opens up new sonic possibilities, providing an immense sonic palette from which you are able to sculpt and craft your own unique sound. As with the rest of these late-90’s Danelectro stompboxes , the Daddy O Overdrive is big, bold and built like an absolute tank. If you have the pedalboard real estate, I highly recommend picking up ALL THREE of these wonderful machines – just this Danelectro trio on a pedalboard can get you almost all the way to where you need to sound for any gig, and at extremely affordable prices. Be sure to check out our reviews for the Cool Cat and Dan-Echo, too, and don’t skip out on our Daddy O demo below – cheers!!
